note: Web fetches hit a session limit partway through, so claims for l08, l09 and a few others are unverifiable. ACOG, NEJM, AJOG and LWW pages were paywalled (402/403), so hosted copies or secondary sources were used where opened.

questions.note: Prior sPTB before 34 wk with CL under 25 mm before 24 wk is a cerclage indication; vaginal progesterone is an option after the 2023 17-OHPC withdrawal.
At age 24, ASCCP 2019 (patients under 25) prefers repeat cytology in 1 year for ASC-US/LSIL, not colposcopy. No choice matches, and colposcopy is only the closest intended answer.
USPSTF reaffirmed this in a June 24, 2025 update; the 2018 date in the stem is outdated but the answer is unchanged.

claims.claim: USPSTF 2021: low-dose aspirin after 12 weeks for those at high risk of preeclampsia (prior preeclampsia, multifetal, chronic HTN, diabetes, renal, autoimmune).
claims.note: USPSTF Sept 28, 2021, 81 mg after 12 weeks. The 12-28 wk, ideally before 16 wk, window is ACOG wording.

claims.claim: Tdap in each pregnancy at 27-36 weeks; RSV vaccine at 32-36 weeks in season.
claims.note: CDC: Abrysvo only, 32 0/7-36 6/7 wk, Sept-Jan.

claims.claim: Live vaccines (MMR, varicella) are contraindicated in pregnancy.
claims.note: Separately, COVID-19 vaccination in pregnancy is attributed to ACOG (correct). Federal HHS/CDC guidance on it changed in 2025; not verified here.

claims.claim: ACOG 2020: aneuploidy screening and diagnostic testing should be offered to all patients regardless of maternal age.
claims.note: Practice Bulletin 226, Oct 2020.

claims.claim: Cell-free DNA is the most sensitive and specific screen for trisomies 21, 18 and 13 and can be done from 9-10 weeks.
Detailed anatomy ultrasound at 18-22 weeks.
ACOG/SMFM 2014: active phase begins at about 6 cm.
claims.note: Obstetric Care Consensus No. 1 (2014).

claims.claim: Earlier Friedman-based standards overdiagnosed arrest; contemporary (Consortium on Safe Labor) data should guide management.
Normal FHR baseline 110-160 bpm; moderate variability 6-25 bpm.
claims.note: Matches NICHD 2008 definitions from memory, but not checked against an opened page.

claims.claim: Second-stage arrest after at least 3 h pushing (nulliparas) and 2 h (multiparas), longer individualised with epidural.
Cesarean for suspected macrosomia considered at EFW of 5,000 g or more without diabetes and 4,500 g or more with diabetes.
ARRIVE (2018): elective induction at 39 weeks in low-risk nulliparas lowered the cesarean rate.
claims.note: 18.6% vs 22.2%. The ACOG 2018 "reasonable to offer" statement was not opened.

claims.claim: 17-OHPC was withdrawn from the US market in 2023 after the confirmatory trial failed to show benefit.
claims.note: FDA final decision April 6, 2023.

claims.claim: Vaginal progesterone is recommended (ACOG 2021) for a history of spontaneous preterm birth or a cervical length under 25 mm before 24 weeks.
claims.note: ACOG and SMFM pages were paywalled. Search snippets suggest the wording overstates: SMFM Consult #70 (2024) uses CL of 20 mm or less for those without prior sPTB, and evidence does not support vaginal progesterone for prior sPTB without a short cervix. The ACOG 2021 attribution looks stale, since PB 234 favoured 17-OHPC for prior sPTB.

claims.claim: Antenatal corticosteroids at 24-34 weeks; magnesium before 32 weeks for neuroprotection.
claims.note: Not checked against an opened page (ACOG pages paywalled).

claims.claim: ACOG 2017 defines PPH as cumulative blood loss of 1,000 mL or more, or loss with hypovolaemia, within 24 h of birth.
claims.note: Practice Bulletin 183, Oct 2017.

claims.claim: WOMAN trial (2017): early tranexamic acid reduces death from bleeding.
claims.note: Benefit when given within 3 h of birth (RR 0.69).

claims.claim: Methylergonovine is avoided in hypertension and carboprost in asthma.
Severe features: platelets below 100,000, transaminases twice normal, creatinine above 1.1 mg/dL or doubled, pulmonary oedema, new headache or visual disturbance.
Severe-range BP should be treated within 30-60 minutes.
claims.note: Acute severe HTN is confirmed as persistent over 15 minutes. The lesson's "two occasions 4 hours apart" applies to diagnosis and must not delay treatment.

claims.claim: CHAP (2022): treating mild chronic hypertension to below 140/90 improved outcomes without impairing fetal growth.
claims.note: Composite 30.2% vs 37.0%; SGA 11.2% vs 10.4% (NS).

claims.claim: Carpenter-Coustan thresholds 95/180/155/140 with two abnormal values; IADPSG 92/180/153 with one.
claims.note: Matches search snippets, but the page fetches failed (session limit).

claims.claim: A2GDM and well-controlled pregestational diabetes are delivered at 39 0/7-39 6/7; A1GDM may await labour to 40 6/7.
claims.note: Not checked against an opened page.

claims.claim: Postpartum 75 g OGTT at 4-12 weeks after GDM, then lifelong screening every 1-3 years.
claims.note: Not checked against an opened page.

claims.claim: Methotrexate for stable unruptured ectopic pregnancy (ACOG 2018), with baseline CBC, liver and renal tests.
claims.note: Web tools hit their session limit before this lesson was checked.

claims.claim: Early pregnancy loss occurs in 10-20% of clinically recognised pregnancies.
claims.note: ACOG cites about 10%; not checked against an opened page.

claims.claim: Intrahepatic cholestasis: ursodeoxycholic acid; delivery at 36-39 weeks depending on bile acids.
claims.note: Not checked against an opened page.

claims.claim: USPSTF 2019 recommends counselling interventions for pregnant and postpartum people at increased risk of perinatal depression.
claims.note: Feb 12, 2019, Grade B.

claims.claim: Zuranolone is approved for postpartum depression.
claims.note: FDA approved Zurzuvae Aug 4, 2023.

claims.claim: ACOG 2018: postpartum contact within 3 weeks and a comprehensive visit no later than 12 weeks.
claims.note: ACOG page paywalled; not opened.

claims.claim: CDC US MEC 2024 update; person-centred, non-coercive counselling.
claims.note: The category 4 list for CHC was not verified on an opened page.

claims.claim: Typical-use failure: LARC and sterilisation below 1%, DMPA about 4%, pill/patch/ring about 7%, condoms about 13%.
Copper IUD is the most effective EC (within 5 days); ulipristal works up to 5 days; levonorgestrel is less effective with obesity.
The FDA approved mifepristone in 2000 for use through 10 weeks of pregnancy.
claims.note: The 2000 approval was through 49 days (7 weeks). The label was extended to 70 days (10 weeks) on March 30, 2016.

claims.claim: Dobbs (2022): no constitutional right to abortion; Roe and Casey overruled; authority returned to the people and their elected representatives.
claims.note: Decided June 24, 2022.

claims.claim: FDA v. Alliance for Hippocratic Medicine (2024): the plaintiffs lacked standing, leaving FDA actions in place.
claims.note: Decided June 13, 2024.

claims.claim: State law varies: some states ban nearly all abortions, others restrict at early gestational ages, with differing exceptions.
claims.note: KFF as of April 1, 2026: 13 states have total bans in effect and 7 have limits at 6-12 weeks LMP. The lesson's 15-week example is not among the current early limits. Exceptions vary: 5 states lack a health exception, 9 lack rape/incest exceptions and 12 lack fatal-fetal-anomaly exceptions. This law changes often.

claims.claim: The 2023 international PCOS guideline allows AMH as an alternative to ultrasound for PCOM in adults.
Letrozole is first-line ovulation induction in PCOS.
Primary amenorrhoea: no menses by 15 with secondary sexual characteristics, or by 13 without breast development.
claims.note: Not checked against an opened page.

claims.claim: ASRM: evaluate after 12 months if under 35, after 6 months if 35 or older.
WHO 2021 semen lower reference limits are about 16 million/mL and 42% total motility.
claims.note: Concentration from a secondary source; the PMC review confirms 42% motility.

claims.claim: Fezolinetant, an NK3 receptor antagonist, was approved in 2023.
claims.note: May 12, 2023. Not checked: newer nonhormonal approvals and FDA action on hormone-therapy labelling may postdate the lesson.

claims.claim: CDC 2021: doxycycline for chlamydia, azithromycin preferred in pregnancy, test of cure in pregnancy.
PID outpatient regimen is IM ceftriaxone plus doxycycline and metronidazole, and an IUD need not be removed.
claims.note: Ceftriaxone 500 mg IM; doxycycline and metronidazole for 14 days.

claims.claim: USPSTF recommends annual chlamydia/gonorrhoea screening for sexually active women under 25 and older women at increased risk.
claims.note: USPSTF 2021 (24 and younger, plus at-risk 25+) supports the groups. It does not specify "annual"; that interval is CDC's.

claims.claim: USPSTF 2018: ages 21-29 cytology every 3 y; 30-65 cytology every 3 y, hrHPV every 5 y or cotest every 5 y; stop after 65 with adequate screening.
claims.note: Still the final USPSTF statement, but a Dec 10, 2024 draft is pending (primary HPV preferred, self-collection allowed). HRSA (Jan 2026) and ACOG (Apr 2026) now prefer primary hrHPV every 5 y at 30-65.

claims.claim: Self-collected HPV samples are approved; guideline bodies are "moving toward" including them; consult current recommendations.
claims.note: Out of date. HRSA/WPSI guidelines (Jan 5, 2026) include patient-collected primary hrHPV at 30-65, with no-cost coverage from Jan 1, 2027. ACOG (Apr 2026) gives a qualified endorsement of self-collection every 3 years where follow-up infrastructure exists. The USPSTF Dec 2024 draft includes it. The lesson should state these.

claims.claim: HPV vaccine: 2 doses if started before 15, 3 doses after 15 or if immunocompromised, catch-up to 26, shared decision-making 27-45 (ACIP).
claims.note: Matches the CDC page dated July 2024. On Jan 5, 2026 HHS/CDC changed the childhood schedule to a single HPV dose without an ACIP vote (SGO, CIDRAP). A federal court put that change on hold in March 2026, and an appeal hearing is set for Oct 6, 2026. The current schedule is in flux.

claims.claim: USPSTF 2018 recommends against ovarian cancer screening in average-risk asymptomatic women.
claims.note: Feb 13, 2018, Grade D.

claims.claim: Lifetime ovarian cancer risk is about 40% for BRCA1 and 15-20% for BRCA2.
claims.note: NCI gives 39-58% (BRCA1) and 13-29% (BRCA2); the lesson figures sit at the low end.

claims.claim: An endometrial thickness of 4 mm or less on TVUS is reassuring in postmenopausal bleeding (ACOG 2018).
claims.note: ACOG page paywalled; not opened.

claims.claim: USPSTF 2024: biennial mammography at ages 40-74.
ACOG recommends offering screening from 40, starting no later than 50, through shared decision-making.
claims.note: Out of date. ACOG's 2024 update says average-risk patients should begin mammography at 40, annually or every 2 years by shared decision-making.

claims.claim: USPSTF (2018) recommends IPV screening of reproductive-age women with referral of those who screen positive.
claims.note: Reaffirmed in a June 24, 2025 update that explicitly includes pregnant and postpartum women. The citation year should be 2025.

claims.claim: CDC 2021 STI prophylaxis after sexual assault is ceftriaxone, doxycycline and metronidazole, with HIV PEP within 72 h.
